Coming from a moderator; that was a tough read. I see a lot of stuff on a daily basis that I really wish I was not exposed to, and none of that compares in the least to what some of the folks in this article run into on a minute by minute basis.

I am not into the tech aspect of this article, but a question came to mind.

Is there any way to turn this type of content removal via real time moderators, into an algorithm/software/ that could prevent the uploading of said content?

I am not sure if such a thing even exists. With all of the data collection companies do, it seems like something practical to keep record of.

As far as I know, there is no such technology (yet) that could replace manual content moderation. People are creative, so if you ban common offensive keywords, for example keyword "fuck", people would just bypass the filter by writing "fuc*k" instead. This one word alone suddenly got hundreds of variations. The same goes for videos, images and audio, the only difference is that the more complex content (video vs a simple keyword), the more complex the algorithm to fight this. It's an endless loop and I am pretty sure there will never be a perfect solution to this problem.
